sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section resolves the apparent contradiction between Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah chapters 3 and 4 regarding whether the revelation of the life-force nullifies or sustains creation, using the analogy of sea creatures versus land creatures.

translations.translation: Now, based on the explanation of the difference between creatures of the sea and creatures of the dry land,
that creatures of the dry land appear as an existence and a separate entity in themselves,
whereas the creatures of the sea do not appear as an existence in themselves,
but rather are utterly nullified to their source of vitality,
the discourse resolves
the apparent contradiction found in Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah.
For behold,
in chapter 3

it is explained how every created being and existence is truly considered as nothing and absolute naught relative to the power of the actor and the breath of His mouth within the acted-upon, which constantly brings it into being and brings it forth from absolute nothing to something, etc.,

and were permission given to the eye to see and apprehend the vitality and spirituality within every created being, etc., the corporeality, materiality, and tangibility of the created being would not be visible to our eyes at all, for it would be utterly nullified in existence relative to the vitality and spirituality within it, since without the spirituality it would be absolute nothing and naught, exactly as before the six days of creation, etc.
Whereas in chapter 4,
regarding the arrangement of the praises of the Holy One, blessed be He—the Great, the Mighty, etc.—
it is explained

that "the Great" is the attribute of Chesed and the diffusion of vitality throughout all the worlds and creations without end or limit, etc., for "Great is the Lord and to His greatness there is no investigation," and therefore He also imparts vitality and bringing-into-being from nothing to something to endless worlds and creations,

and the attribute of His might, the Holy One, blessed be He, is the attribute of tzimtzum, etc., that the vitality is hidden within the body of the created being, and it is as if the body of the created being is a thing in itself, etc.
And superficially they contradict each other,
for in chapter 3 it implies that the revelation of the vitality
(were permission given to the eye to see)
causes the nullification of the existence of creation,
whereas in chapter 4 it implies the opposite,
superficially,
that the revelation of the vitality
(the attribute of Chesed and the diffusion of vitality)
is the sustenance of the existence of all created beings from nothing to something,
for the efflux of vitality and bringing-into-being from nothing to something to endless worlds and creations comes only from the attribute of Chesed,
whereas the concealment and hiding is from the attribute of Gevurah,
and its effect is only that the created being is felt as a thing in itself,
and if so,
even when the tzimtzum and concealment from the attribute of Gevurah are removed,
so that there will be a revelation of the vitality,
there will be a true existence and reality for all created beings from nothing to something,
and not as implied in chapter 3, that with the revelation of the vitality the existence of the created beings will be nullified.
However, the explanation of the matter will be understood based on what was explained above regarding the difference between creatures of the dry land and creatures of the sea,
that creatures of the dry land appear as an existence in themselves,
but not so creatures of the sea, whose existence is nullified and covered by the waters of the sea,

and this is also the explanation of what is stated in chapter 3, that were permission given to the eye to see, etc., the corporeality of the created being would be utterly nullified in existence, etc.,
that the intention is not that when the tzimtzum is removed there will be an absence of the existence of the created beings,
or a loss of existence,
absolute nothing and naught exactly as before the six days of creation,
but rather,
that the existence of the created beings will be in ultimate nullification relative to their source,
like the light of the sun when it is within the body of the sun's sphere, which is nullified in existence and considered as absolute nothing and naught
(as explained there in the continuation of the discussion),
and this means,

that with the removal of the tzimtzum, all created beings will be nullified in existence relative to their source, analogous to creatures of the sea, whose existence is not apparent because it is nullified and covered by the waters of the sea,
as water covers the sea.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that souls descend from being like sea creatures in the hidden world to being like land creatures in the revealed world, and the purpose of this descent is to achieve the same nullification to G-dliness even in the revealed world through the meditation on the oneness of G-d in the Shema.

translations.translation: Now, although the souls of Israel before their descent below are in the category of creatures of the sea,
in the hidden world,
nevertheless,
in their descent below to the revealed world to be clothed in bodies,
they become included among the creatures of the dry land, which appear as an existence and a thing in themselves,
to the extent that there is a need for the Torah's command, "And you shall choose life,"
from which it is understood that they have free choice to do the opposite of good, G-d forbid,
and concerning this the Torah commanded that they choose true life, etc.
And the ultimate purpose of the descent of the souls below,
is that even when they are below in the revealed world, being like creatures of the dry land that appear as an existence and a thing in themselves,
there should be within them nullification to G-dliness in the manner and likeness of the nullification of the creatures of the sea in the hidden world.
And this matter is accomplished through meditation on the first verse of the Shema,
"Hear O Israel, the Lord our G-d, the Lord is One,"
specifically "One,"
and not "Alone,"
as explained above,
that "One" means that there is an existence of worlds, except that they are nullified to His oneness, may He be blessed,
and as is hinted in the word "Echad" (One),
that the seven firmaments and the earth
(eight)
and the four directions of the world
(four)
are nullified to the Master of the world
(one).
And this is why the intention in the first verse of the Shema is indispensable
(that if one did not intend, he has not fulfilled his obligation),
because the intention and meditation on the matter of "One" is the ultimate purpose of the soul's descent into the body,
to effect that even below there should be nullification to G-dliness.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two types of knowledge—upper knowledge where the lower is considered nothing relative to the higher, and lower knowledge where the lower feels itself as something—and that the service is to achieve the nullification of the upper knowledge even in the revealed world through the supernal unity of the Shema.

translations.translation: And the matter is,
for it is written,
"G-d of knowledge is the Lord,"
"knowledge" [implies] two,
upper knowledge and lower knowledge.
Upper knowledge is that above is "yesh" (existence) and below is "ayin" (nothing),
and this means,
that even though the existence of the lower is a true existence,
for it is written,
"In the beginning G-d created the heavens and the earth,"
and "G-d created" implies the seal of truth,
and moreover, the entirety of the fulfillment of the Torah and mitzvos is specifically below,
from which it is proven that this is a true existence,
nevertheless it is called "nothing,"
because the existence of the lower is considered as nothing relative to the Divine light which is the source of life, which is therefore called "existence."
And this is the knowledge of the hidden world,
where its creatures feel their source of vitality,
and therefore the nullification to their source of vitality is felt by them,
that their existence is nothing relative to their source of vitality, which is the existence.
And lower knowledge is that below is "yesh" (existence) and above is "ayin" (nothing),
this being the knowledge of the revealed world,
where its creatures do not feel that their source of vitality is the Divine light that brings them into being and gives them life,
and therefore it is called by them "nothing,"
because it does not shine within them in revelation but in concealment and hiding,
and because of this they feel themselves as an existence and a separate entity.
And the service is that even below, in the revealed world, there should be the matter of nullification as it is from the aspect of upper knowledge,
and this is the matter of the supernal unity in the first verse of the Shema.
